correctness.rationale: The operator K_a has the complete L2 sine basis of the Dirichlet–Neumann boundary problem. Its eigenvalues and the Doob conjugation are directly integrated, giving all Q eigenmodes. For each x>-1 the relative one-step density is L2 and its spectral coefficients are nu_m f_m(x); Parseval bounds the nonleading modes by 5^-n and 7^-n. Absolute-mode integrals give the exact TV constants. The f1 zero x=1/3 is unique and f2 there is -1. Strict positivity of the two-step density proves stationary uniqueness. The finite checker independently reproduces 233 finite assertions, not the infinite spectral theorem.

value.rationale: The mathematical gap is the relaxation of a probability law conditioned on arbitrarily long persistence, a natural stochastic-dynamical observable distinct from persistence probability. A unique starting innovation cancels the dominant mixing mode and switches the sharp TV exponential base from 1/3 to 1/5. Exact constants, uniqueness, and parameter universality identify a coherent structural phenomenon rather than a routine renaming or isolated finite computation.
